content: To apply eye drops, first wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses while using this medication. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above the eye and place one drop into the pouch. Afterward, look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eyes. Do not rinse the dropper after use. If you are using other types of eye medications, such as drops or ointments, wait at least 5 minutes before applying the next medication. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results, and continue using it for the full duration prescribed, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. This medication may cause temporary stinging or burning in the eyes for a minute or two after application. Other possible side effects include temporary blurred vision, eye discomfort, itching, redness, dryness, tearing, a sensation of something in the eye, or sensitivity to light. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because its benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to a new fungal eye infection. Do not use it for longer than prescribed. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before using ofloxacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other quinolones (such as ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (such as preservatives like benzalkonium chloride) that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. After applying this medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred or unstable. Use caution when driving or operating machinery until your vision stabilizes. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not contain all possible drug interactions. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another condition unless directed by your doctor. Discard any unused medication after completing your treatment. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature. Discard the solution if it changes color, becomes cloudy, or develops particles. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
